item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Nobody doesn't have to be necessarily the Critic. The old Nobody had power in a lot of institutions so these need new placements. And the new Nobody isn't doing much of anything yet

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: What an incredible piece, I thank you for taking the time to create it and I applaud you for your creativity. I am simply struck by your ability to come up with so many works of art. Conceiving a single skip is hard enough but you described an entire gallery of them. I envy your imagination.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: God DAMN. That was… extraordinary. To be quite honest, it felt like I was reading a novel in its own right, and that, I think, is what a tale should be. +1 a thousand times over.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Bravo my friend this is truly amazing and was a wild ride from start to finish. I loved every single moment of it. Even though I felt bad for Ruiz I think it was a fitting end for a troubled young man. Not sure how I feel about Carol being the janitor but hey I'll roll with it.

Overall though I felt it was an excellent wrap up to the best series I've read on this site.

+1

item.title: Necrosis
item.content:encoded:
Best I can figure:
But only Randomini knows for sure.

Failed. Was not killed. Reset/Reborn. Some of me wonders if he's 076-2. He's tried multiple forms of suicide. God heard, but did not stop him. Yet he lives.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Best collection of short fiction I've read in a very long time. The Foundation isn't even the setting, it's just the vehicle by which you're telling this amazing story. This could stand on its own, no problem.

Extremely well done.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Probably one of the best books (if you'd call this a book?) I've ever read. Second only to maybe The Outsiders. I loved it. The random alliteration in the dialogue, the multiple twists, the bookending, parallelism, the shout-outs and references…oh man, I loved it.

I'm really curious as to how you made something this amazing. How long have you been writing for? Do you write a lot?

I'm not sure if I should be more angry with you for that, or for not having the entire rest of the 'verse published already because now I want to read it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I've read novels shorter than this series. It's too goddamn much. There's so much subtle stuff going on. I want to reread it to find all the little Easter Eggs and such, but I'll never be able to make the time to do that. Holy hell. +1'd hard.

The suicide sections are so unclear that they seem to not even matter at all to the story and thus should be cut as being extraneous. The best I can figure is that they're Pico talking to the voices in his head about the times he tried to kill himself and then… what? Gave up trying?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
wowwee indeed

I like that Ruiz's eulogy went tragically unheard.

I like that Felix ended up the new Critic.

I kind of forgot a lot of the details along the way that would have made this a truly stupendous conclusion, but I trust you knew what you were doing and I enjoyed it nevertheless.

Also, almost every instance of "lied" in this piece needs to be "laid". Or maybe "lay".

item.title: E: Now that I've read them all.
item.content:encoded:
Well then. That was a wild ride.

The ending between Mr. Redd and Isabel was fantastic, though I might be a little biased in that regard.

e: On the whole, I would say that the edgy tryhard awcy-type artist got a bit tiring after a while over the course of this series, and the Mr. Redd subplot seemed a bit…extraneous? Unnecessary? like it could have been a separate tale and little would have been lost.
